info.description:
The **Trainer Prediction System** ranks Uganda Police Force trainers against training
programme requirements and produces an auditable allocation record.

### What this system is

A **decision support system** using deterministic weighted multi-criteria decision
analysis. Five criteria — specialisation match, proven performance, years of service,
qualification, and availability — are normalised to a common 0–100 scale, weighted by a
policy an administrator controls, and summed.

It is **not** machine learning. There is no trained model, no probability, and no
prediction of future events in the statistical sense. Every score decomposes into
per-criterion contributions that a human can read and defend, which is precisely what a
learned ranker could not provide. See `docs/ALGORITHMS.md` for the full reasoning,
including the alternatives that were considered and rejected.

### Reading the numbers

- **`predictionScore`** — a 0–100 weighted total. Comparable *within* one prediction
  run; not meaningful across runs with different weights.
- **`confidenceLevel`** — how much the system **knows about this trainer**, not how
  likely they are to succeed. A trainer with no evaluation history scores LOW
  confidence however strong their qualifications. This is the most misread number in
  the interface.

### Authentication

Sign in at `POST /api/v1/auth/login` to receive a bearer access token (15 minutes) and
a refresh token (7 days). Send the access token as `Authorization: Bearer <token>`.
Rotate at `POST /api/v1/auth/refresh` before expiry.

### Errors

Every error — including validation failures — is
[RFC 9457](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9457) `application/problem+json`, carrying
a `requestId` that matches the `X-Request-ID` response header. Quote it when reporting
a problem.

post.description:
**This is the decision.** BR-02 restricts it to a Training Administrator and BR-06 requires it to be explicit — there is no auto-approve and no bulk approve anywhere in this API.

In one transaction the server verifies the candidate comes from the current ranking, **re-checks the hard gates against live data** (a trainer may have become unavailable since the run — 409 if so), freezes the score, breakdown, rank, weights and rationale, draws a registry number, sets the allocation `PENDING_TRAINER`, moves the programme to `AWAITING_RESPONSE`, notifies the trainer, and writes the audit entry (BR-07).

`weights` and `weightsWereSimulated` in the body are accepted for compatibility and **ignored** — the frozen weights come from the run itself, because a receipt whose figures were supplied by the client could be made to say anything.

201.description: Approved. The Decision Receipt is the response body.

403.description: Only a Training Administrator may approve (BR-02).

409.description: The ranking is superseded, the requirements changed since it was generated, the programme already has an allocation, or the candidate no longer passes the gates.

get.description:
The frozen snapshot: score, breakdown, rank and weights **as they stood at approval**, the rationale the trainer was shown, the approving officer with their rank, the registry number, the trainer's response, and the linked evaluation if one exists.

None of it is recomputed. An evaluation recorded next month changes future rankings; it must not change the justification for a decision taken today.

post.description:
Authenticates a username (or email) and password, returning a short-lived access token and a rotating refresh token.

**Account lockout (FR-01).** Three consecutive failures lock the account for 15 minutes and return `423` with `retryAfterSeconds`.

**No user enumeration.** A wrong password and an unknown username return the identical message. Do not rely on the wording to detect whether an account exists — it is deliberately uninformative.

**Deactivated accounts** receive a distinct `403`, because a deactivated user retyping a correct password forever helps nobody.

get.description:
Returns the authenticated user with their role, rank, and — when they are a Trainer — their `trainerId`, which the frontend uses to route to self-service screens.

Account status is re-read from the database on every request, so a user deactivated moments ago is rejected immediately rather than when their access token happens to expire.

post.description:
Exchanges a valid refresh token for a new access + refresh pair, revoking the presented token.

**Reuse detection.** Presenting a token that was already rotated revokes every token in the same family and returns `401`. That pattern means the token was captured — the legitimate holder would be presenting the newest one.

401.description: The token is unknown, expired, or already used.

Runs the **identical engine** with override weights and **persists nothing** except a `WEIGHTS_SIMULATED` audit entry.

Weights must total 100 (422 otherwise). The response has the same shape as a real run, plus `rankDeltas` showing how the top candidates moved against the stored ranking.

Same code path as `POST /programmes/{id}/predict` by design — a separate simulation implementation is how a preview silently diverges from what the server would actually produce.

200.description: The simulated ranking and rank movements.

403.description: Only a Training Administrator may simulate.

422.description: The weights do not total 100, or a criterion is unknown.

get.description:
Paginated and filterable. Search matches title **or** registry number.

The list is **not scoped by creator** — officers see all programmes, because training is coordinated across a directorate rather than owned by whoever typed the request.

post.description:
FR-04. Creates a programme at `DRAFT` with a generated registry number.

Requirements are **not** accepted here — FR-05 defines them separately via `PUT /programmes/{id}/requirements`. Keeping the two apart is what makes the `DRAFT` → `REQUIREMENTS_SET` transition a real event.

403.description: Only officers and administrators may raise requests.

delete.description: Only from `DRAFT` or `REQUIREMENTS_SET`. Anything further along has allocation history that forms part of the decision record and returns 409 — cancel it instead, which preserves the record.

409.description: It has allocation history; cancel instead.

get.description: With its lifecycle timeline, latest prediction run, and allocation count.

patch.description: Blocked with 409 once the programme is `ALLOCATED` or beyond — a trainer has accepted a commitment by then, and moving the dates would silently change what they agreed to.

409.description: Too far along to edit.

get.description:
Runs the **gates only** and returns counts: *"142 of 812 trainers meet these criteria."*

Cheap by construction — no scoring, no narrative. Its purpose is to let an officer discover that their criteria are too narrow **before** spending a prediction run, rather than after staring at a list of three names.

409.description: Requirements are not yet defined (FR-05).

post.description:
FR-06. Runs the engine over every trainer, persists the run, marks prior runs superseded, clears the re-run flag, and moves the programme to `PREDICTED`.

**409 if requirements are undefined** — FR-05 forbids proceeding without them, because the engine would have nothing to match on and would rank the entire force.

Prior runs are superseded rather than deleted: what the system recommended, and when, is part of the audit record.

409.description: Requirements are undefined, or no scoring policy is active.

get.description:
The latest non-superseded run: ranked candidates with their score breakdowns, rationales, confidence, and counterfactuals.

**Always ordered by rank. There is no `sortBy` parameter** — BR-05 fixes the order, and letting a client re-sort would let the interface present a different recommendation from the one recorded.

404.description: No ranking has been generated yet.

put.description:
FR-05. `requiredSpecializationAreaId` is required; minimum experience and qualification are optional.

Moves `DRAFT` → `REQUIREMENTS_SET`. **If a ranking already exists**, sets `requirementsChangedSincePrediction` and audits `REQUIREMENTS_CHANGED` — that flag raises the amber re-run banner, because the ranking on screen was computed against different criteria and approving from it would mean approving against requirements that no longer apply.

409.description: The programme is past the point of redefinition.

get.description: Returns all ten reference lists together. Preferred over the individual endpoints when a screen needs more than one — the programme form needs six, and one request is better than six.
get.summary: Every lookup list in one response

get.description: How a course is run — Refresher, Induction, Pre-Deployment — which is a different axis from what it is *about*. A Refresher course may be about Cybercrime Investigation; see `/reference/specializations` for subject.

get.description:
Is delivery getting better or worse? Filterable by category and specialisation.

These are **raw** means, not the shrunk figures the prediction engine uses. A quarter's mean is a description of what happened; the engine's shrinkage exists to stop a single evaluation dominating a *ranking*, which is a different job.

200.description: One row per quarter, oldest first.

get.description:
**This is the report that holds the system to account.** A ranking engine that keeps surfacing the same six names is working exactly as designed and failing at the purpose, and this is where that becomes visible.

Trainers with **no** allocations are included deliberately — an empty row is the finding. A report listing only busy people cannot show who is never used.

`region` filters on the **trainer's posting**, not the course venue: the question is which postings are being drawn on, not where courses ran.

200.description: Rows, a chart of the busiest ten, and the filters used.

get.description:
Server-side CSV via `StreamingResponse` — the file is never materialised in memory. `reportType` is `utilisation` or `allocation-history`.

The export is audited as `REPORT_EXPORTED`, with the filters that produced it.

Serves the permission matrix as **data**, so the Roles screen is not a hard-coded table in the frontend that has to be edited in two places to stay true — and would therefore eventually be true in one.

schema.title: Response List Roles Api V1 Roles Get

200.description: The roles, with user counts and permissions.

get.summary: The four roles and what each may do

get.description:
Weights, labels, plain-English descriptions, and who last changed them.

The descriptions are stored on the row rather than in the frontend, so an administrator retuning a weight can also correct the sentence that explains it without waiting for a release.

409.description: No policy is active.

put.description:
NFR-10. Creates a **new version** and deactivates the previous one — it never mutates in place.

That matters because every prediction run stores the weights that produced it. Editing a policy in place would leave historical rankings explained by weights that were not in force when they were generated, which is the difference between an auditable decision and one that merely looked right at the time.

All five criteria are required and must total exactly 100.

200.description: New version adopted; the previous one is deactivated.

403.description: Only a System Administrator may change the weighting.

422.description: The weights do not total 100, or a criterion is missing.

get.description: With effective dates and authors, so an old ranking can be explained.

schema.title: Response Policy History Api V1 Scoring Policy History Get

get.description:
`elapsedMs` for recent runs, with the ten-second NFR-01 threshold and a count of breaches.

The chart matters because degradation here is gradual: the pool grows, a query plan flips, and the run that took 200 ms takes four seconds — still inside the budget, and still the signal that something changed.

403.description: System Administrator only.

get.summary: Prediction run times against the NFR-01 budget

get.description:
Failed sign-ins and unauthorised attempts in the last 24 hours, accounts currently locked, live sessions, and deactivated accounts.

`failedNotifications` is included on purpose: a notification that silently did not arrive is worse than one that visibly did not, so delivery failures surface here rather than being swallowed.

403.description: System Administrator only.

get.summary: Security figures for the System Health screen

get.description:
Paginated, filterable directory. `search` matches name **or** force number via trigram indexes, so partial and mid-word matches work.

Returns a projection rather than full profiles — call `/trainers/{id}` for credentials and history.

403.description: Trainers cannot browse the directory.

get.description: The caller's trainer record, derived from the bearer token. There is no `userId` parameter by design — identity comes from the token, never from the request.

403.description: This account has no linked trainer profile.

patch.description:
FR-02. Rank, station, years of service, contact number, and biography.

**Rank, station, and contact number cannot be set empty** — a blank value returns 422 naming the field, rather than storing a blank where a phone number was.

403.description: This account has no linked trainer profile.

422.description: A required field was blank or out of range.

get.description:
Pending invitations, confirmed upcoming courses, and past assignments.

Each pending item carries `frozenRationale` — **the trainer is entitled to see why they were selected**, not merely that they were.

post.description: Confirms the assignment, records the response time, moves the programme to `ALLOCATED`, sets the trainer `ASSIGNED` — which caps their AVAILABILITY score on future runs, so the system stops favouring someone already committed — and notifies the approving Administrator.

403.description: That assignment belongs to another trainer.

409.description: It is no longer awaiting a response.

post.description:
**A reason is required** — 422 without one, and a database `CHECK` refuses any declined row that lacks it. The Administrator is notified with the reason and the next-ranked candidate's name, and the programme returns to `PREDICTED` so that candidate can be promoted from the same ranking.

BR-07: the decision is audited whether it was an approval or a refusal.

403.description: That assignment belongs to another trainer.

409.description: It is no longer awaiting a response.

patch.description: Marking yourself `AVAILABLE` is refused with 409 while you hold a confirmed allocation for a course that has not yet finished — you cannot be committed to a course and open for another at the same time.

409.description: A confirmed allocation is still in progress.

get.description: Every evaluation recorded against you, with the mean.
Return the caller's qualifications.

post.description: FR-03. **Appends** — it never overwrites an existing entry. A POST that replaced the list would silently delete a record of a degree still held.

409.description: The year obtained is in the future.

delete.description: Object-level check: 403 if the qualification belongs to another trainer.

403.description: It belongs to another trainer.

get.description: Return the caller's specialisations.

schema.title: Response My Specializations Api V1 Trainers Me Specializations Get

post.description:
FR-03. `proficiencyLevelId` is **required** — a missing level is a 422, never a defaulted BASIC, because a defaulted proficiency would feed the scoring engine a number nobody stated.

A duplicate discipline returns **409, not a silent update**: quietly overwriting would let a trainer downgrade their own recorded level with no trace.

409.description: That discipline is already recorded.

delete.description: Object-level check: 403 if it belongs to another trainer.

403.description: It belongs to another trainer.

get.description: Return the caller's absence windows.

schema.title: Response My Unavailability Api V1 Trainers Me Unavailability Get

post.description: Leave, court, deployment, study, or medical. Overlapping windows are refused with 409 — you cannot be on leave and in court at the same time, and an overlap would double-count against the availability gate.

409.description: It overlaps an existing window.

422.description: The end date precedes the start date.

delete.description: Remove one of the caller's absence windows.

403.description: It belongs to another trainer.

get.description:
Credentials, declared absences, and evaluation history.

A Trainer may fetch **only their own** record; staff roles may fetch any. This is the object-level check that role gating alone cannot express.

403.description: A Trainer requested someone else's record.

get.description: Also reachable as `/evaluations/trainer/{trainerId}`. This path exists because the frontend already calls it.

403.description: A Trainer requested someone else's history.

get.description:
Filterable by role, account status, and free text over username, name and email.

Returned in the standard paginated envelope. There are forty-odd accounts today, but *every* list endpoint uses the envelope — an unpaginated list is a latent problem waiting for the system to succeed.

403.description: System Administrator only.

post.description:
Creates the account with a **generated** temporary password and `mustChangePassword = true`.

The caller does not choose the password. An initial password chosen by an administrator travels by whatever channel they use to pass it on, and is very often reused.

If the role is `TRAINER`, the linked trainer profile is created **in the same transaction** — a Trainer account without a profile cannot see assignments and cannot be ranked, which is a broken state that must be impossible rather than merely unlikely. `stationId` and `forceNumber` are therefore required for that role.

`temporaryPassword` is in the response body **once**. It is never logged, never stored in plaintext, and cannot be retrieved again.

201.description: Created. The temporary password is shown once.

403.description: System Administrator only.

409.description: The username or email is already in use.

422.description: A trainer account was submitted without a posting.

get.description: Return one user.

patch.description:
A **role change takes effect at the next sign-in** — the role travels in the access token. Rather than leave that as a surprise, the response says so, and the user's refresh sessions are revoked so the change lands within the access token's fifteen-minute lifetime rather than at its leisure.

`accountStatus` accepts `ACTIVE` or `SUSPENDED`. Deactivation has its own endpoint because it must also revoke sessions.

403.description: System Administrator only.

409.description: The email is taken, deactivation was attempted here, or this is the last active System Administrator.

post.description:
Sets `DEACTIVATED` and **revokes every session immediately**. A deactivated user cannot sign in with the correct password, and cannot continue on an access token issued a minute ago — the account status is re-read from the database on every request precisely so revocation is immediate.

**The last active System Administrator cannot be deactivated** (409), and neither can your own account.

409.description: Already deactivated, your own account, or the last administrator.

post.description: Issues a new temporary password, sets `mustChangePassword`, clears any lockout, and revokes every session. The password is shown once.

200.description: Reset. The temporary password is shown once.

get.description: Reports that the process is running and able to serve a request. Does **not** touch the database — a liveness probe that fails when a dependency is down causes the orchestrator to restart a container that was working correctly.

Reports whether the service can handle traffic, by executing `SELECT 1` against PostgreSQL.

**If this reports the database as unreachable from inside the container**, the problem is almost always host networking rather than the application. On Linux, `host.docker.internal` requires `extra_hosts: ["host.docker.internal:host-gateway"]` in Compose, PostgreSQL listening on the Docker bridge address, and a `pg_hba.conf` rule permitting `172.16.0.0/12`. See §3.3 of the database prompt, and diagnose with:

```bash
docker compose exec backend python -c \
  "import socket; print(socket.gethostbyname('host.docker.internal'))"
```

503.description: At least one dependency is unreachable.

get.description: Version, commit, and environment. Used by the frontend's About panel.
